summary: Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981) and held posts at the University of Milan (~1993) and the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University (attested 2003) under supervisors Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, and was taught by Chongren, Xiaoxun, Zhiben, and Xuewen He, and Xi Aniu.

Eric George Hart (1878–1946) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Victoria College, Jersey, and Wellington College, he served as Professor of Arabic, Persian and Hindustani and Reader of Indian History at Trinity College Dublin from 1926 to 1938.
Eric Haruki Swanson works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held posts at Loyola Marymount University and at Stanford University as a Senior Visiting Scholar (attested 2026).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Manchester and Uppsala under Bengt Sundkler, later serving as Reader at Lancaster, First Chair of Religious Studies at Sydney (1977–1996), and Professor at Uppsala (1978–1981).

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He held posts at San Francisco State University (2023) and Yale University (attested 2017 and 2026).

Eric Moses Gurevitch works in Indology and history/archaeology. He was an NEH Postdoctoral Fellow at Vanderbilt University (attested 2023) and an Assistant Professor at Harvard University (attested 2025).

Eric P. Hamp (1920–2019) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Amherst and Harvard (~1946–1954) under Joshua Whatmough. He held long-term academic appointments at the University of Chicago (~1950–1991) and the University of Michigan.

Eric Steinschneider works in Indology and religious studies. Mentored by Srilata Raman, he has served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Ithaca College (attested 2022–2026).

Eric Stephen Goodell specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed MA degrees at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Eric Thomas Stokes (1924–1981) was a historian who earned his Ph.D. at Cambridge under Thomas George Percival Spear. He taught at Malaya, Bristol, and Zimbabwe before serving as Smuts Professor of History at Cambridge (1970–1981).

Eric Villalobos works in religious studies and Indology. He has been affiliated with the Graduate Division of Religion and studied as a doctoral student in Asian, African, and Middle Eastern Religions at Emory University (attested 2026).

Erica Baffelli is a scholar in Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and serves as Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Manchester (attested 2016, 2026).
Erica Biagetti is a scholar working in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. She earned her PhD from the University of Pavia by 2021 and has held an academic post there.

Erich Arno Lehmann (1901–1984) worked in Indology and religious studies, receiving a Dr.Theol. from the University of Leipzig (~1946–1947). He held posts at Leipzig (~1950–1951), Halle-Wittenberg (Dean, 1950–1966), and the University of Jena (~1951–1966).

Erich Berneker (1874–1937) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leipzig under August Leskien. He served as professor at the German University in Prague (1902–1909), the University of Breslau (1909–1911), and the University of Munich (1911).

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Austrian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger. He spent his career at Vienna as Direktor (1939–1945) and Professor (1955–1964).

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held professorships at Berlin (1920–1925, 1932–1945), Leipzig (1925–1931), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel (1912–2000) was a philosopher who earned his Dr. phil. (~1931–1936) and habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He later served there as außerordentlicher Professor (1952) and ordentlicher Professor of Philosophy (1960–1982).
